question: Deal or no deal?

lines.text: Trump has rejected Iran's seven-day plan to reopen Hormuz, the Wall Street Journal reports.
lines.note: WSJ via Reuters / Al Jazeera, 26 Sep

lines.text: US officials told the paper Trump is sceptical that Iran would meet his demands.
A US official told Al Jazeera Washington is in no hurry to respond.
lines.note: Al Jazeera / Anadolu via A News, 26 Sep

lines.text: Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, says the next move is America's.

scene.quote: The choice now rests with the United States.

lines.text: His plan: fighting stops on every front, including Lebanon and Yemen.
The US would release about twelve billion dollars in frozen assets, lift oil sanctions and end its blockade.
Then, on day seven, Hormuz would reopen.
President Masoud Pezeshkian says the plan was coordinated with Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, state media reports.
lines.note: Arab News (Reuters), state media on CBS interview, 26 Sep

lines.text: But in an interview with Al Jazeera, he says Iran does not trust Washington.

scene.quote: We have no trust in the American side

lines.text: Our running number: Kpler data shows just nine ships crossed Hormuz on Thursday.
Before the war began on 28 February, it was about 125 a day.
At the UN, Bahrain says it rejects any permit or fee to pass through the strait.
lines.note: Anadolu via Middle East Monitor, 25 Sep UNGA

lines.text: Day 211 of the war, and the strait is still waiting on Washington.
Deal or no deal? Day 212 tomorrow.
